message.content:
Build **persisted error logging + an admin Error Logs view** for the Nxeon platform at /opt/nxeon (Next.js App Router + Prisma + Postgres + serial job worker). Goal: anything that goes wrong on the customer side, or internally, is captured and visible to admins — instead of vanishing into stderr.

## Current state (verified by a mapping pass — reliable)
- `lib/log.ts` is THE single error choke-point: `logEvent(level, context, detail)` and `logError(context, error, extra)` currently write a structured JSON line to STDERR only + a best-effort POST to `NXEON_ERROR_WEBHOOK` if set. NOTHING is persisted to the DB. The docblock literally calls it "the single choke point" for a future sink. This is where you add DB persistence — do it once here and EVERY existing and future `logError` call is captured automatically.
- Callers of logError today: `app/api/log/route.ts` (the client error-boundary sink — `app/error.tsx`/`app/global-error.tsx`/`app/admin/error.tsx` POST here; rate-limited 20/min/IP), `lib/actions-blog.ts`, `lib/actions-testimonials.ts`, `lib/actions-newsletter-campaign.ts`. `console.error` is used ad-hoc elsewhere (not your job to convert all — but see below).
- Existing DB-persisted failures already surfaced in `app/admin/logs/page.tsx` (3 tabs: Audit=AuditLog, Activity=merged AuditLog+WalletTransaction+Job [FAILED jobs shown with j.error], Email=EmailLog): `Job.error`/`Job.status=FAILED` and `EmailLog.error`/`status`. Your new Errors view should COMPLEMENT these, ideally unifying "things that went wrong" (ErrorLog + failed Jobs + failed EmailLogs) into one admin surface.

## Schema is ALREADY in the DB + client generated — do NOT edit prisma/schema.prisma
Use `ErrorLog`: id, level[error|warn|info], source[worker|action|api|client|job], context, message, detail?, fingerprint (UNIQUE), userId?, serverId?, jobId?, count, firstSeen, lastSeen, resolved. Dedup: identical repeated errors must bump `count`+`lastSeen` via a fingerprint upsert, NOT insert a new row each time.

## What to build
- **`lib/log.ts` (edit — you OWN it):** add DB persistence to `logError`/`logEvent`. Compute a stable `fingerprint` = hash(context + normalized message) (strip volatile bits like ids/timestamps/hex from the message before hashing so the same error dedups). Upsert on fingerprint: on conflict bump `count` and `lastSeen` (and refresh `detail`/`level` if you like); else insert with firstSeen=lastSeen=now. Persistence MUST be best-effort and NON-FATAL: wrap in try/catch so a DB hiccup never breaks the caller (this is a logger — it must never throw). Keep the existing stderr + webhook behavior. Accept optional `source`/`userId`/`serverId`/`jobId` via the `extra` arg. Beware recursion: if the DB write itself fails, do NOT call logError again — just console.error.
- **`lib/actions-errors.ts` (new, `"use server"`, ADMIN-gated):** list errors (paginated, filter by level/source/resolved, newest by lastSeen), mark-resolved / mark-unresolved, and optionally a unified feed combining ErrorLog + recent FAILED Jobs + failed EmailLogs. All exports `requireArea("platform")` (matches the current logs page gating) INSIDE each function.
- **`app/admin/logs/page.tsx` (edit — you OWN it):** add an "Errors" tab (`?tab=errors`) beside Audit/Activity/Email. It shows the ErrorLog feed: level badge, source, context, message, count ("×N"), first/last seen, affected user/server/job links where present, and a resolve toggle. Make failed things scannable (red for error, amber for warn). Keep the existing 3 tabs working.
- **`components/admin/ErrorLogViewer.tsx`** — client component for the interactive list (filters, resolve toggle, expand detail/stack).
- **A few high-value capture points:** wire `logError(...)` into the MOST important currently-silent customer-facing failure catch sites that you OWN or can add one line to WITHOUT touching another stream's files. Priority: the client error boundary already flows through api/log→logError (good, now persisted). Do NOT edit `worker/index.ts` (I wire the job-failure capture centrally — tell me in your report the exact `logError` call you want at the worker's job-failure catch). Do NOT edit files owned by other streams (app/dashboard/sites, worker/monitor.ts, lib/monitoring.ts, app/admin/backups, app/admin/monitoring, app/status).
- **`test/error-log-*.test.ts`** — tests that bite: fingerprint normalization/dedup (same error → same fingerprint; volatile ids stripped), the upsert-bumps-count logic (factor the fingerprint fn as pure + testable), and source tripwires proving `lib/log.ts` persists and every `lib/actions-errors.ts` export authenticates.

## Files you OWN (only these)
- `lib/log.ts` (edit)
- `lib/actions-errors.ts` (new)
- `app/admin/logs/page.tsx` (edit — add Errors tab, keep the rest)
- `components/admin/ErrorLogViewer.tsx` (new)
- `test/error-log-*.test.ts`

## Files you must NOT touch (report instructions instead)
- `prisma/schema.prisma` (frozen), `worker/index.ts` (I wire job-failure capture — give me the exact logError line), `lib/admin-groups.ts`/`lib/rbac.ts` (the /admin/logs nav entry already exists; if you only add a ?tab=errors you need NO nav change — confirm this in your report), and every other stream's files listed above.

## Platform rules (non-negotiable)
- The logger must NEVER throw and never recurse on its own failure.
- `"use server"` = every export is a public endpoint; `lib/actions-errors.ts` exports must `requireArea("platform")` INSIDE each function. Resolving/reading errors is admin-only.
- Do not leak secrets: if a message/detail could contain tokens, follow the existing redaction pattern (there's an EmailLog token-redaction test in test/ — mirror that spirit; scrub obvious secret-looking substrings before persisting).
- Tests must bite: `stripCommentsAndStrings`/`stripComments` from `test/_source-tools.ts` for source tripwires. Prove the dedup with real assertions.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean for your files; `npm test` (node:test).
- Do NOT run prisma db push/migrate, next build in place, git commit, deploy, systemctl.

## Deliver
Typechecking code + tests. Final report: (1) the exact `logError(...)` line you want added at worker/index.ts's job-failure catch (so job failures flow to ErrorLog with source="job", jobId, serverId); (2) confirm no nav change needed (tab-only); (3) the fingerprint strategy; (4) test count; (5) what you wired vs left as future capture points. Report is data for me.

2	import type { Role, User } from "@prisma/client";
3	import { realUser } from "./auth";
4	
5	/**
6	 * Role-based access control for the admin ops portal.
7	 *
8	 * The admin surface is divided into logical *areas*. Each area maps to the set
9	 * of staff roles allowed to see and use it. ADMIN implicitly has every area.
10	 * The admin layout uses this to (a) let any staff role in and (b) hide nav
11	 * items a role can't reach; each sensitive page additionally gates itself with
12	 * `requireArea(...)` so a hand-typed URL is refused too.
13	 */
14	export type Area =
15	  | "overview"
16	  | "analytics"
17	  | "clients"
18	  | "support"
19	  | "fleet"
20	  | "billing"
21	  | "platform";
22	
23	/** Which roles may access each area. ADMIN is always allowed (see canAccess). */
24	export const AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]> = {
25	  overview: ["SUPPORT", "BILLING", "ADMIN"],
26	  analytics: ["ADMIN"],
27	  clients: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
28	  support: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
29	  fleet: ["ADMIN"],
30	  billing: ["BILLING", "ADMIN"],
31	  platform: ["ADMIN"],
32	};
33	
34	export function canAccess(role: Role, area: Area): boolean {
35	  return role === "ADMIN" || AREA_ROLES[area].includes(role);
36	}
37	
38	/** Any non-customer role that belongs in the ops portal. */
39	export function isStaff(role: Role): boolean {
40	  return role === "SUPPORT" || role === "BILLING" || role === "ADMIN";
41	}
42	
43	/** Maps admin nav hrefs to their governing area. Unknown routes default to platform (ADMIN-only). */
44	const HREF_AREA: Record<string, Area> = {
45	  "/admin": "overview",
46	  "/admin/analytics": "analytics",

94	/**
95	 * Server-side page guard. Redirects to /login if signed out, or back to the
96	 * overview if the (staff) user's role can't reach this area. Returns the real
97	 * signed-in user (impersonation is refused elsewhere in the admin layout).
98	 */
99	export async function requireArea(area: Area): Promise<User> {
100	  const user = await realUser();
101	  if (!user) redirect("/login");
102	  if (!isStaff(user.role)) redirect("/dashboard");
103	  if (!canAccess(user.role, area)) redirect("/admin");
104	  return user;

The database is confirmed, so I'm moving forward with the build. I'm designing a fingerprinting function that hashes the context and normalized message together, where normalization strips out volatile elements like hex sequences, digit patterns, timestamps, ISO dates, UUIDs, and CUIDs to create stable error signatures.

Now I need to decide where to persist logs—logEvent is the choke point since logError delegates to it, so I'll persist there. This means all logEvent calls (info, warn, error) will be logged to the database, which the schema supports through the level field. I'll persist only error and warn level events to keep the table meaningful and avoid polluting it with informational success messages like "newsletter.campaign.sent". Now I need to handle redaction — scrubbing secret-looking substrings from message and detail fields before persisting, similar to how email redaction works.

I'm creating a redaction function that strips secret query parameters like token, code, key, secret, otp, invite, auth, signature, password, pw, api_key, and access_token, plus Bearer tokens and password assignments. I'll keep it focused on query params and Bearer tokens to avoid over-engineering. Then I need to normalize the fingerprint by stripping volatile bits like UUIDs.

Writing normalization function... IP addresses would get normalized to `<n>.<n>.<n>.<n>` anyway through the number replacement, so that's fine. I'll compute the fingerprint as a SHA256 hash of the context plus normalized message, taking the full hex string for the unique column. These utility functions need to live in a shared location like `lib/log.ts` so tests can import them, though that module will also need to import the database client.

The tricky part is that importing `lib/log.ts` in tests will pull in the Prisma client through the `@/lib/db` import, but I need to verify that `tsx` respects the tsconfig path aliases when running tests. Looking at how the existing email-render test handles this — it imports modules that likely use the `@/` alias themselves, so the path resolution should work fine.

For the actual tests, I need to avoid triggering real database connections. The fingerprint function should be pure and testable on its own, so I'll focus on verifying that identical errors produce the same fingerprint (proving the dedup key works) and that volatile IDs get stripped consistently. Then I'll add a test that confirms the upsert logic increments the count correctly.

Since lib/log.ts imports the database client at the top level, the import itself is safe—PrismaClient construction doesn't establish a connection until a query runs. The logger is server-only (called from the API route, not the client error boundary), so there's no risk of pulling Prisma into the browser.

Now I'm writing lib/log.ts with the new functions: a pure `errorFingerprint` function that takes context and message, a `normalizeForFingerprint` helper, and optional `redactSecrets` export for testing. The `logEvent` function needs to extract source, userId, serverId, and jobId from the detail object for the ErrorLog table columns, while storing the remaining fields like stack, digest, and path as JSON.

For the source field, I'll default to "action" when unspecified since that's the primary caller, though callers can override via extra.source. The detail JSON will contain everything from the original line except the columns we're breaking out, and I'll redact secrets from both the message and detail before persistence.

Writing persistence logic... Writing redaction patterns...

For the server actions, I need to set up `listErrors` to handle filtering and pagination with area authorization, `setErrorResolved` to update the resolved status and revalidate the admin logs path, and optionally a `unifiedFailures` function that aggregates errors across logs, failed jobs, and failed emails—though the main feed will focus on the error log entries.

The viewer component will manage filter state client-side and call `listErrors` via `useTransition` to refetch when filters change, while the initial rows render server-side so the page works without JavaScript. I'll make sure `listErrors` returns serializable data with dates converted to ISO strings.

Now I need to enrich the error rows with user and server details—resolving user IDs to emails and server IDs to display names by querying those tables based on the IDs present in the error logs.

Everything is complete and verified. Here is my final report.

## Final report

**What shipped** (only my owned files; all typecheck-clean, `npx tsc --noEmit` reports 0 lines):
- `lib/log.ts` — `logEvent` now persists to `ErrorLog` at the single choke point (so every existing/future `logError` is captured). Best-effort, non-fatal (`persist()` swallows all errors and falls back to `console.error`, never re-entering the logger). Exposes pure, testable `normalizeForFingerprint`, `errorFingerprint`, `redactSecrets`.
- `lib/actions-errors.ts` (new, `"use server"`) — `listErrors` (paginated, filter by level/source/resolved, newest by `lastSeen`, enriches user email + server name since `ErrorLog` has no FK relations), `setErrorResolved`, and `unifiedFailures` (ErrorLog + FAILED Jobs + failed EmailLogs merged). Every export calls `requireArea("platform")` as its first line.
- `app/admin/logs/page.tsx` — added the `?tab=errors` tab beside Audit/Activity/Email; existing three tabs untouched.
- `components/admin/ErrorLogViewer.tsx` (new client component) — level/source/resolved filters, ×N count, first/last seen, user/server/job links, expandable detail, resolve toggle via the admin-gated action.
- Tests: `test/error-log-fingerprint.test.ts` (8) + `test/error-log-persistence.test.ts` (6).

**(1) Exact `logError` line for `worker/index.ts`** — add inside the terminal-failure branch `if (!retriable) { … }` (around line 1145, after `reconcileFailedJob`), so only genuinely-failed jobs (not transient retries) create rows. `error` there is already root-password-redacted and clipped to 2000 chars:
```ts
await logError(`job.${String(job.type).toLowerCase()}`, new Error(error), {
  source: "job",
  jobId: job.id,
  serverId: job.serverId ?? undefined,
});
```
Requires `import { logError } from "../lib/log";` (or your `@/lib/log` alias) at the top of `worker/index.ts`. This dedups per job-type + normalized error, with `source="job"`, `jobId`, `serverId` populated.

**(2) No nav change needed — confirmed.** `/admin/logs` already exists in `HREF_AREA` (platform, ADMIN-only) in `lib/rbac.ts`. `?tab=errors` is only a query param on that same route, so no nav entry and no rbac edit.

**(3) Fingerprint strategy.** `fingerprint = sha256(context + "\n" + normalize(message)).slice(0,40)`. `normalize` lowercases and collapses volatile substrings to placeholders in strict order so a broad pattern can't eat a narrow one: UUID → cuid (`c[a-z0-9]{20,}`) → long hex (`[0-9a-f]{16,}`) → ISO timestamp → IPv4 → any digit run (`\d+`, no word boundaries so `5000ms`/`42%` are caught) → whitespace-collapsed. Same incident across different ids/timestamps/servers dedups to one row; `context` is part of the key so the same message under a different context stays separate. Upsert keys on the unique `fingerprint`: on conflict it bumps `count: { increment: 1 }` + `lastSeen` and refreshes level/message/detail; else inserts with `firstSeen=lastSeen=now`. Messages/details are run through `redactSecrets` (token=/password/Bearer/etc.) before persisting. Info-level events are skipped so `ErrorLog` stays a failure store.

**(4) Test count: 14** (all pass). 8 fingerprint tests (dedup determinism, cuid/uuid/timestamp/ip/number stripping, context sensitivity, bounded hex, redaction) + 6 source tripwires (upsert-with-count-increment present, persistence lives in the `logEvent` choke point not `logError`, catch falls back to `console.error` and never re-enters the logger, info skipped, every `actions-errors` export guarded by `requireArea`, every guard is `"platform"`). Full suite: 670 tests, 669 pass — the one failure (`auth-lockouts.test.ts` "B4 schema… additively") is pre-existing and unrelated (I touched no schema/auth files).

**(5) Wired vs. future.** Wired now: the client error-boundary path (`app/error.tsx`/`global-error.tsx`/`admin/error.tsx` → `api/log/route.ts` → `logError`, already `source:"client"`) now persists; and every existing `logError`/`logEvent` caller (`actions-blog`, `actions-testimonials`, `actions-newsletter-campaign`) auto-captures via the choke point.
